AWPTCM-T33323.objective:
• A policy-map can be modified (e.g., class contents changed) while attached to an interface or LAG without first detaching it.
  • Dynamic changes to an attached policy-map take effect immediately with no error, are visible in show commands, and correctly affect ongoing traffic.
  • Dynamic policy-map changes work on static and LACP LAG interfaces.
  • Dynamic policy-map changes work on VCS stacks, including during master failover or member disruptions, without causing instability (no memory leaks, high CPU, etc.).
  • When hardware classifier tables are full, further dynamic additions to the policy-map are rejected with an appropriate error; configurations within the limit continue to work correctly.
  • Basic QoS (ACL/class-map/policy-map) setup continues to function correctly before and after dynamic updates.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability. Primary coverage from TestLink DPMAP family (AWP-20971 primary dynamic change, AWP-20974 while traffic running, AWP-21187 LAG, AWP-21053 VCS, AWP-20975 HW limit). ART coverage from 1331 (policy re-attach, storm QoS attach, large QoS on LAG/VCS no crash) + 1344 (class-map + policy with policer).

Configure QoS with ACL/class-map/policy-map and apply to interface. Send traffic. Change class contents of the policy-map without detaching. Verify show reflects change, no error, and traffic uses updated policy.
Repeat the dynamic change while traffic is continuously flowing; confirm immediate effect and continued correct QoS behavior.
Apply and dynamically change policy-map on a static LAG and on an LACP LAG; verify operation.
On a VCS stack (with LAG across members), dynamically change policy-map during normal operation and during VCS disruption (e.g. failover). Confirm stability and correct updated behavior.

Configure QoS until HW filter limit is reached. Attempt further dynamic additions to policy-map/class/ACL without detaching; verify rejection with error. Confirm working policy within limit still functions.
